svg.text: CodePulse on AWS ECS Fargate: Network Architecture
Task SG: 3001 from ALB SG only
Task SG: 3001 from ALB SG only
RDS SG: 5432 from Task SG only
DB subnet group spans both AZs
OIDC role, no stored AWS keys
build, push image, deploy to ECS
DB URL, JWT secret, Claude API key
Cost mode (default, use_nat = false): no NAT gateway. Tasks run in the app subnets with a public IP and reach ECR, logs and the Claude API
directly through the Internet Gateway. Inbound is still locked down: the Task SG only accepts traffic from the ALB SG.
Production mode (use_nat = true): app subnets become private and outbound traffic goes through the NAT gateway (one NAT here to save cost;
production would run one per AZ). Security group chain in both modes: Internet to ALB SG (80/443), ALB SG to Task SG (3001), Task SG to RDS SG (5432).
The stack is torn down with terraform destroy between demos and rebuilt from code with terraform apply.
AWS WAF on the ALB: AWS managed rule groups + rate-based rule
Known web attacks, request floods, API cost abuse
Security group chain: ALB SG to Task SG (3001) to RDS SG (5432)
Direct access to tasks or the database
DB subnets have no internet route; RDS publicly_accessible = false
Any network path to the database
Prisma parameterized queries, JWT auth, per-user ownership checks
SQL injection, users reading others' data
Least-privilege Postgres user for the app (no DROP, no admin)
Limits damage if something gets through
Secrets Manager for app secrets; GitHub OIDC, no stored AWS keys
Leaked keys in code, images or CI
ECR scan on push for container image vulnerabilities
CloudWatch alarms on ALB 5xx and WAF blocks; Claude API spend limit
Not noticing an attack or runaway cost
